prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production mobile UI artwork sprite atlas, transparent background. Create exactly THREE separate illustrated activity symbols in a single horizontal row. Wide 3:1 canvas preferred. Three equally sized square cells; each symbol is centered at x=1/6, 1/2, 5/6 of canvas width and y=1/2 of canvas height. Left is a BLUE WATER DROP representing puppy pee; middle is a warm OCHRE/BROWN POOP COIL with NO FACE representing puppy poop; right is a GREEN DOG FOOD BOWL containing a few brown kibble pieces representing eating. Exactly these three objects, no other separate objects, no labels, no lettering, no numbers, no emoji. Each object fits inside 70 percent of its cell width and inside the CENTRAL HORIZONTAL STRIP whose height equals one third of the total canvas width. Large transparent gaps between objects, equal apparent visual weight. Clean silhouette and very few details so recognizable at 30 pixels. Each object must be entirely isolated on alpha, no common background, no cast shadow outside its own small silhouette, no panels or enclosing sheet. They must look like a complete bespoke illustrated icon family made for an adult puppy diary app, not stock emojis. All objects on exactly the same baseline. Art direction PUPPY JOURNAL: hand-painted watercolor and irregular dark ink outlines on lightly torn paper cutouts, like small hand-made diary stickers. Soft cornflower blue #497AB9 waterdrop with one tiny ink shine dash, warm ochre #A97037 poop coil with simple rounded stacked outline, leaf green #558351 dog bowl with offwhite rim and simple small paw stamp on front. Warm ivory paper edge only 2–3 percent of object size; organic imperfect silhouettes and subtle watercolor pigment inside each shape. Elegant gentle illustration for grown-up dog owners. Flat artwork, restrained ink texture, no shiny 3D, no faces, no gradients of light, no huge white sticker border. Avoid the generic phone emoji silhouette; give the waterdrop a slight lean, the coil a small rounded base, and the bowl a hand-thrown asymmetrical ceramic lip.
